warnings: Two dummy x-lines both naturally anchor to main grid '1' (one before the origin at x=-1.725, one between grid 1 and grid 2 at x=2.375). Spec precedent (house #04) names a before-origin dummy '1'' with negative pos_m; the between-1-and-2 dummy also anchors left to grid '1' per the direction rule. Applying the prime-ordering rule (scan left-to-right, first found = 1 prime) since both anchor to the same base grid: x=-1.725 is encountered first -> '1\'', x=2.375 is encountered second -> '1\'\''. This is a judgment call, not an explicit spec example — flagged for review.

A small circular symbol with 4 diagonal lines radiating to the bay corners appears at the center of every bay on the grade-beam plan (หน้า21, right view, 'แปลนคานระดับอะเส'). Text inside the circle is illegible even at 5x zoom. Not a recognized element_type from the closed vocabulary and no clear structural role (does not sit on a grid intersection). Excluded from elements[] on the ring-beam plan file rather than guessed — possibly an M&E coordination symbol (floor drain / grounding point) copied onto the structural sheet from a shared template.

z_levels: no sheet within op04 scope (S-01 through S-11) prints a metric value (e.g. '+0.60') next to the level labels 'ระดับอะเส' / 'ระดับพื้นชั้น 1' / 'ระดับที่กำหนด' — those labels are used as reference datums in S-05/S-10/S-11's column schedules and S-06/S-07's pile-cap sections without an accompanying printed elevation number on any structural sheet. The architectural sheets (A-01 to A-16) likely carry the actual finished-floor-level elevation but are out of op04 scope. z_levels[] is left empty rather than inventing values.

unassigned_dimensions.note: Small dimension printed immediately beside footing F(0.60x0.80)/pile-mark F2 at grid ref C1'. Exact meaning unresolved (possibly a Y-axis eccentricity of the footing centroid off the C row line, common for an edge/corner footing). Does not change the footing's recorded grid_ref (C1'), which is read from the clearly-printed 1.725 chain instead.

dummy_grid_rule_check.negative_pos_m: Dummy x-line before the x=0 origin (grid '1') is at x=-1.725; per the house #04 precedent this keeps the id '1\'' rather than taking over the origin, with a negative pos_m.
dummy_grid_rule_check.prime_ordering: Two separate dummy x-lines both anchor to grid '1' (one before it, one between it and grid '2'). No spec example covers two dummies anchored to the same base grid in different gaps; resolved by scanning left-to-right across the whole x-axis and assigning primes in the order encountered: x=-1.725 -> '1\'' (1st), x=2.375 -> '1\'\'' (2nd). See warnings[].
